standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard calculus of partial derivatives in a polynomial ring: the derivative of an element of the square of an ideal lies in the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the fact that the two partial derivatives of the given quadratic element lie in the ideal, which drives the first case distinction.

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the derivation used in characteristic two to produce elements of the ideal of a controlled shape.

standard_prerequisites.name: Freeness of the conormal module of the auxiliary ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard description of the conormal module of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of two elements in a two dimensional situation

core_obligations: First case (proof lines 3327-3349): the partial derivatives of the given quadratic element lie in the ideal; if one of them is nonzero a linear change of coordinates makes the first variable lie in the ideal, so the ideal is either principal generated by that variable or generated by it together with a monic polynomial of degree at least two in the other variable; in the first case the claim is immediate and in the second every element of the square of the ideal has the displayed shape with coefficient functions, and a degree comparison forces the two nonconstant parts to vanish and the remaining factor to be constant.

Characteristic two case (proof lines 3351-3390): if both partial derivatives vanish one is in characteristic two and the element reduces to a combination of the two squares; after rescaling one may assume the element is a sum of one square and of a coefficient times the other square; if the coefficients are squares one is done, and otherwise a derivation taking a nonzero value on one of them can be extended to the polynomial ring and used to show that the ideal contains a polynomial of the form constant plus a square, and combined with the original relation that it also contains the other such polynomial.

Excluding the last possibility (proof lines 3390-3396): the auxiliary ideal generated by those two elements has conormal module free of rank two, so the inclusion into the given ideal is strict, which produces an element of the given ideal whose quadratic part has a nonzero mixed coefficient; among such elements one can be chosen with vanishing linear part, and a dimension count then shows that the ideal has the shape with colength three, a case in which a direct reduction (or a change of coordinates after passing to the algebraic closure) shows that the original quadratic element cannot lie in the square, completing the proof.
proof_roadmap: Use the partial derivatives to reduce the first case to an ideal containing a coordinate, and compare degrees inside the square of the ideal.
In the remaining case work in characteristic two, where the element is a combination of squares, and use derivations to force a polynomial of the shape constant plus square into the ideal.
Rule out the resulting configuration by showing the inclusion of the auxiliary ideal is strict and by a dimension count on the quotient.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a nonzero quadratic polynomial in two variables with field coefficients lies in the square of an ideal of colength greater than one, then that quadratic polynomial is a scalar multiple of a square of a linear polynomial (statement lines 3315-3325). The proof (proof lines 3327-3398) analyses the partial derivatives and reduces the first case to an ideal containing a coordinate where degrees can be compared, treats the characteristic two case through derivations of the field, and rules out the remaining configuration by a conormal module argument and a dimension count. H3: a case analysis with a genuine characteristic two argument, written out in full.
